findings.passage: People should be able to vote without photo identification.
findings.note: Questionnaire statement in the section 'Elections and Voting' of the iVoterGuide candidate questionnaire, with the ticked answer 'Strongly Disagree'. The page shows the answers for the Kentucky general election of November 8, 2022 (State Rep., Dist. 66); the date the answer was given is not shown.

findings.passage: Photo identification is a very simple and fair means to confirm identity. It is a necessary measure to help to insure secure elections, and it is not unfair to anyone.
findings.note: His written comment under the photo-identification questionnaire statement in the 'Elections and Voting' section; the page shows the answers for the 2022 general election race (State Rep., Dist. 66).

findings.passage: I am an advocate for the elimination of electronic voting systems, and for a return to paper ballots and hand counting. For election security, no machine should be connected in any way to the internet. I would propose laws be passed to keep all private companies and private individuals out of the election process. Private money, which was part of the 2020 election voter fraud, should not be permitted. Mail in voting should not be allowed other than limited absentee voting. Elections should be held on one day only. There are many other voter integrity measures that could be put in place.
findings.note: His answer to the questionnaire question 'What laws would you propose to change present voting practices?' It covers voting machines, private money in elections, mail voting limited to absentee, one-day elections and other voter-integrity measures. The page shows the answers for the 2022 general election race (State Rep., Dist. 66).

findings.passage: I believe it is crucial that only U.S. citizens vote in elections. After all, we are the ones who live here, follow the laws, and care about what happens.
findings.note: From a column explaining the 2024 constitutional Amendment 1 (SB 143), which would bar anyone who is not a U.S. citizen from voting in Kentucky. The column is published on a county committee's site; the page's description names Rep. Steve Rawlings (District 66) as the author.

findings.passage: Before I continue, I want to emphasize that there have been no reported cases of non-citizens voting in Kentucky elections.
findings.note: Same 2024 column on Amendment 1 (SB 143); he states that no cases of noncitizen voting have been reported in Kentucky.

findings.passage: HB 139 modernizes Kentucky’s election laws by raising campaign contribution limits, improving election administration, tightening voter ID rules, and allowing data sharing with federal agencies to verify voter eligibility.
findings.note: In his Week 12 legislative update (signed Sen. Steve Rawlings, District 11, published on a county committee's site), this is his description of HB 139, listed among measures that advanced through the Senate that week. It describes the bill; it does not say how he voted.
